title: Flutter desktop resource fixture memory measurements

measurementScope.comparisonCheckpoints: nearest external process sample to fixture closed round 5, closed round 20, and final idle UTC times
measurementScope.peakScope: all captured external samples in each completed process lifetime, including startup and workload phases

excludedAttempts.reason: Process exited without a fixture report; startup-only measurements cannot establish workload completion.

aggregate.privateBytesFinding: Closed-round values fluctuate. All post-warmup OLS slopes are positive; final-idle endpoint changes have mixed signs. Slow sustained growth is unresolved by these short fixture runs.
aggregate.handlesFinding: Closed-round handle counts fluctuate without a strict per-round increase; final-idle endpoint changes are small and have mixed signs.

limits: The measurements cover the memory-check Release resource fixture snapshot, not the final installed desktop package.
Each completed run has 20 resource cycles, five warmup cycles, a five-second idle after each close, and a final 60-second idle; this is not a per-cycle 60-second idle acceptance test.
Resource fixtures replace Host traffic; real model conversations, account login, plugin services, network reconnection and prolonged Computer Use are outside the measured workload.
Empty resource-owner and Flutter image-cache counters establish closure of instrumented resources; process Private Bytes can retain engine, allocator and native caches without instrumented owners.
Three short process lifetimes cannot establish the absence of all long-term memory leaks.
External peaks are sampled peaks; a 250-millisecond nominal sampler can miss shorter peaks.
One launch without a fixture report is excluded and retained separately; the cause is unknown.
